statement: The premise the inherited research document was sized against — small models "achieve 94%+ syntactic validity with ~0% semantic correctness" — is false on the half that carried the argument. Measured on identical stored completions (n=164 per corpus, five corpora, HumanEval+ greedy): syntactic validity by ast.parse is 100% for qwen2.5-coder 1.5B/3B/7B and qwen3-coder-30b-a3b and 98.2% for gpt-oss-20b, while semantic correctness on the same rows is 65.2% / 80.5% / 82.9% / 88.4% / 53.7% — not ~0%.

citations.supports_because: The per-completion rows the syntactic rate is computed from — one line per task with its ast.parse verdict, unaggregated, so the rate can be recomputed rather than trusted.

EvalPlus per-task pass/fail for the 1.5B, run over the same stored completions the syntactic rate was measured on. Measuring both rates on identical rows is the only way the 94%/~0% claim is even well-formed, and no prior run did it.
The original generation run's own summary, which independently reports the same HumanEval+ pass rates and so rules out the re-evaluation having produced them.
The rig, commit-pinned: the `premise` subcommand that produced both halves. It re-runs from a checkout, which is what makes the number reproducible rather than reported.

_confidence_note: High for what it measures, and deliberately narrow. HumanEval+ is self-contained single-function synthesis — the easiest shape a code model faces — so this BOUNDS the inherited claim and does not generalise to repository-situated contract work, where semantic correctness will be lower. Its independent check is that the three qwen2.5-coder figures reproduce data/capability-table.json (0.652 / 0.805 / 0.829) to three decimals from a separate rig run, which is why confidence is high despite one benchmark family. What this record does NOT establish is a replacement premise: the correct reading is that the inherited number was never evidence, not that 65-88% is the semantic rate for contract work. See ADR-0004 — the ordering that premise was used to sort is the thing that needs re-deriving, and that is not settled here.
